Write SCENE LS1 (1 of 5) of a natural Japanese LISTENING conversation between two people for a learner.
WHOLE CONVERSATION: two friends meet, catch up and talk about everyday things (food & cooking, plans & schedule, shopping & payment)
SPEAKERS: A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · A and B are friends talking; natural spoken Japanese in one consistent register.
REGISTER: natural spoken · friendly
THIS SCENE: A and B meet and start talking about today
ONE CONVERSATION — the learner hears ONE continuous conversation; this request writes its next PART (part 1, internal only — never announce it).
CONVERSATION CONTRACT: speakers A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · relationship: adult friends · opening location: where they meet · objective: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → do / eat / buy → pay · ending goal: they finish what they set out to do and say goodbye
STORY SO FAR: (nothing yet — this part opens the conversation)
NEXT PART GOAL: see THIS SCENE above.
- Do NOT say goodbye: the conversation continues afterwards. End this part on an answer or a statement, not on an open question.
LATER PARTS will use: ここ, そこ, 大丈夫, どこ, 好き, すみません, たぶん, 今日, 明日, これ, 見る, ありがとう, 帰る, 飲む, 食べる, 話す, する, ちょっと, 買う, いくら, お金, 会う, 来る (leave them for later).
SCENE INTENT: WHO the same two friends throughout · WHERE where they meet · SITUATION A and B meet and start talking about today · WHY they talk: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → do / eat / buy → pay · WHAT they want to achieve: A and B meet and start talking about today. Every turn moves this goal on; a target that does not fit the goal is used in a short natural aside, never a random topic jump.
SCENE RELATIONSHIP: adult friends · EXPECTED REGISTER: plain / friendly everyday Japanese (track speech style NATURAL)
CONTEXT SO FAR: this is the opening scene — start with a natural greeting
SCENE SHAPE: the exchanges pursue the scene goal; the scene ENDS with that goal resolved (they decide, agree, pay, or say goodbye). Lesson words are heard inside real talk — never a list of sentences about each word.
CLOSED WORLD — PRIORITY ORDER: 1. use ONLY the vocabulary listed here · 2. use every required target · 3. correct grammar · 4. the learner level · 5. be natural WITHIN those limits. Naturalness never justifies a word that is not listed.
THIS SCENE MUST USE ALL OF THESE 7 REQUIRED TARGET WORDS (id | word [reading] | meaning | role) — every one must appear in the actual text of a turn:
T35 | 友達 [ともだち / tomodachi] | friend | CONTENT
T20 | どう [どう / dou] | how | QUESTION_WORD
T24 | ある [ある / aru] | exist | ACTION
T25 | いる [いる / iru] | exist | ACTION
T2 | 行く [いく / iku] | go | ACTION
T15 | 分かる [わかる / wakaru] | understand | ACTION
T9 | 一緒 [いっしょ / issho] | together | CONTENT
ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY (already taught — the ONLY other content words you may use; any inflected form of them is fine): いい (good) · それ (that) · 一 (one) · うん (yeah) · 家 (house) · 知る (know) · 何 (what) · あれ (that over there) · いいえ (no) · はい (yes) · 今 (now) · 本当 (really) · 始める (start) · 入る (enter) · 出る (leave) · 欲しい (want) · 思う (think) · 何時 (what time) · 作る (make) · いつ (when) · 誰 (who) · なんで (why) · 持つ (hold) · 十 (ten)
ALLOWED GRAMMAR / FUNCTION WORDS (particles, copula, inflection, sentence endings): は が を に で と も の へ か ね よ な や から まで より だけ しか って ので のに けど けれど し とか ばかり くらい ぐらい ごろ など だ です だった でした じゃ じゃない じゃなかった ではない ではありません じゃありません でしょう でしょ だろう だろ ます ました ません ませんでした ましょう ない なかった たい たかった た て てる ている ています ていた てた ちゃう ちゃった れる られる そう よう らしい みたい ん んだ んです ください かな かね よね だよ だね よな わ さ ぞ ぜ っけ でも だから それで そして それから では この その あの どの えっと えーと うーん ええ ああ あっ えっ へえ ほら そっか たら こんにちは うん またね じゃあ
You may use ONLY: 1. the required target words · 2. the allowed support vocabulary · 3. the grammar / function words. Do NOT introduce any other lexical content (no other noun, verb, adjective, adverb, interjection or name). If an idea cannot be said with these words, SIMPLIFY THE IDEA — never improvise a new word.
TURN PLAN — MEANING FIRST, VERBALIZABILITY PROVEN (validated before this call; say each planned turn in this order, with exactly this meaning; at most ONE extra short reaction may be added between planned turns):
PROVEN FRAME = a sentence already checked for this learner (every word authorised, within the length limit, the lesson word present): say it like this or as a natural variant with the SAME words, and keep the track register.
  T1 A QUESTION(how it is) — A asks B how it is (using どう "how" + 友達 "friend") · REQUIRED: どう "how" + 友達 "friend" · SUPPORT: いい それ あれ 一 うん 家 · PROVEN: 友達、どう？
  T2 B ANSWER — B answers with how it is ⟨must give how it is⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: いい それ あれ 一 うん 家 · PROVEN: いいね。
  T3 A QUESTION(yes/no) — A asks B a yes / no question (using ある "exist") · REQUIRED: ある "exist" · SUPPORT: いい それ 一 うん 家 知る · PROVEN: それ、ある？
  T4 B ANSWER — B answers with yes / no (or a qualified answer) ⟨must give yes / no (or a qualified answer)⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: いい それ 一 うん 家 知る · PROVEN: うん、ある。
  T5 A QUESTION(place) — A asks B where (a place) (using いる "exist") · REQUIRED: いる "exist" · SUPPORT: 家 あれ いい それ 一 うん · PROVEN: どこにいる？
  T6 B ANSWER — B answers with a place (using 一緒 "together") ⟨must give a place⟩ · REQUIRED: 一緒 "together" · SUPPORT: 家 あれ いい それ 一 うん · PROVEN: 一緒に家にいる。
  T7 A QUESTION(place) — A asks B where (a place) (using 行く "go") · REQUIRED: 行く "go" · SUPPORT: 家 あれ いい それ 一 うん · PROVEN: どこに行く？
  T8 B ANSWER — B answers with a place ⟨must give a place⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: 家 あれ いい それ 一 うん · PROVEN: 家に行く。
  T9 A QUESTION(yes/no) — A asks B a yes / no question (using 分かる "understand") · REQUIRED: 分かる "understand" · SUPPORT: いい それ 一 うん 家 知る · PROVEN: 分かる？
  T10 B ANSWER — B answers with yes / no (or a qualified answer) ⟨must give yes / no (or a qualified answer)⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: いい それ 一 うん 家 知る · PROVEN: うん、分かる。
PLAN: exchange 1: A uses どう+友達, then B replies · exchange 2: A uses ある, then B replies · exchange 3: A uses いる, then B uses 一緒 · exchange 4: A uses 行く, then B replies · exchange 5: A uses 分かる, then B replies
ROLE GUIDE: CONTENT = the topic of a turn · QUESTION_WORD = a question the other speaker answers · ACTION = what someone does or will do
LENGTH: 10–11 turns. HARD MAXIMUM 11 turns.
EACH TURN: CURRENT LEVEL: Shodan · PREFERRED LENGTH: 4–16 Japanese content units · ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM: 20 Japanese content units (polite / question / sentence-final particles do not count). Prefer 4–16 — the shortest natural way to say it. Use 17–20 only when the idea or the lesson word cannot be said naturally more simply. Never exceed 20. A short natural reply ("yes", "okay", "really?") is fine — never pad a line. If a speaker needs to say more, split it into another turn. Keep the situation simple enough to say at this level — one idea per turn (e.g. "How much is it?" / "Ten thousand baht." / "That is expensive."), never explanations in one long turn.
RULES:
- Each turn is ONE speaker; questions get answers; never put a question and its answer in the same turn; A and B both speak.
- At most 3 lesson words per turn (the required words above AND these other lesson words count: 大丈夫, 今日, 食べる, 好き, 飲む, どこ, する, ちょっと, 来る, 明日, ありがとう, すみません, 見る, 買う, いくら, お金, ここ, そこ, これ, たぶん, 帰る, 会う, 話す).
- Response words (yes / no / yeah …) are used as REPLIES. No repeated sentences. No filler turns that do nothing.
- Do not say goodbye yet; the conversation continues in the next scene.
- Content words ONLY from the required targets and the ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY above. No personal names.
TRACK SPEECH STYLE: NATURAL (Natural — Friendly everyday Japanese).
REGISTER: NATURAL (default).
Natural adult conversational Japanese: predominantly PLAIN forms, friendly and socially considerate.
This is NOT textbook Japanese with ます removed — write it as natural speech from the start.
PREFER: plain verb forms, subject omission, natural word order, contractions (てる/ちゃう/んの), sentence-final particles (ね/よ/の/かな), softening (と思う/かも), natural fragments.
AVOID: recurring です/ます/ですか/ますか where the social context does not demand it. A little is fine if genuinely warranted; do not drift back into textbook-polite Japanese.
PROHIBITED: rough speech — お前, てめえ, だぜ, ぞ (assertive), じゃねえ, うるせえ, 食え (bare imperative).
NOT anime caricature, not aggressive male speech, not teenage slang overload.
Example style: 今日は何する？ / これ食べてみる？ / ちょっと高いね。 / たぶん大丈夫だと思う。
Each scene states its RELATIONSHIP and EXPECTED REGISTER — follow them: same relationship ⇒ same register all the way through (no drifting between です/ます and plain forms).
